$schema_note: Podcast Production Engine (Skill 58) RUNTIME model-resolution policy. SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for how runtime models are SELECTED. This file prescribes NO model by name. Selection resolves in strict order: (1) the client's explicit choice for the task (a per-call model_choice, or the PODCAST_MODEL_CHOICE / PODCAST_CONTENT_MODEL / PODCAST_QC_JUDGE_MODEL env labels), then (2) the client's configured default model, recorded per tier under models.client_defaults in the CLIENT's own models config (located by the router's existing config search: explicit path, then the PODCAST_MODELS_JSON env label, then this shipped file). If neither resolves, the router STOPS with a clear ask-the-client message (exit 5): it never substitutes a named model silently. Anthropic models are BUILD-TIME ONLY and NEVER ship here (PRD Section 3.3; furnace-design Guardrail 5): the router refuses any model id matching deny_patterns, including a client-chosen or client-configured id, as a HARD ERROR, never a silent fallback, and every substitution is logged in the delivery report. models.providers is a capability registry (provider lanes, base urls, credential ENV LABELS only, never a secret value) used to complete a client-named model into a callable lane. Recommendation, offered as guidance the client can override: a high-reasoning model for content work, because episodes are long-form generation in the client's own voice, and a judge model DISTINCT from the writer model, because the writer never grades its own work as the deciding vote. guard-no-anthropic-runtime.py reads this file at the merge gate and asserts: the selection policy is present with the ask-the-client stop, deny_patterns are armed, and any configured entries are deny-clean with a judge model distinct from the content model.

models.$guard_exemption_note: The strings inside deny_patterns are REFUSAL tokens, NOT model usage. There is ZERO Anthropic model id, provider, key, or host CONFIGURED for use anywhere in this file: no Anthropic base_url, no Anthropic API key env is read, no Anthropic API host is called. These six bare tokens are matched case-insensitively as substrings at runtime, so they also refuse any Anthropic package slug, key-env label, or host that embeds one of them (for example any string containing 'anthropic'). deny_patterns is the denylist SOURCE that guard-no-anthropic-runtime.py itself consumes; the guard treats this array as its own denylist declaration and never as an Anthropic reference (furnace-design Guardrail 5 ships exactly this six-token list in the runtime config).

client_defaults.$note: The client's configured default model per tier, recorded in the CLIENT's own copy of this config from the client's answer at install time. SHIPPED STATE: null (unset) for both tiers; this shipped file deliberately names no default. An entry is one link object or a list of link objects; a link may omit base_url / api_key_env when its provider is listed in models.providers, and the router completes it from that registry.

deny_match.note: Any model id, provider slug, package, host, or env key matching a deny pattern is refused as a HARD ERROR at runtime, never accepted as a fallback or substitution.

ollama-cloud.note: Subscription lane. ollama-cloud needs baseUrl slotting, not apiKey slotting (ollama-cloud-baseurl-trap). NEVER route content through the local signed-in daemon.

openrouter.note: Pay-per-token lane. Model ids on this lane keep the vendor prefix (vendor/model). live_verify the exact slug at canary.

client_choice.per_call: route context key model_choice: a provider-qualified model id string (ollama/<model>:cloud, openrouter/<vendor>/<model>, gemini/<model>) or a full link object {provider, model, base_url, api_key_env, ...}

client_configured_default.block: podcast_engine.models.client_defaults.<tier>: one link object, or a list of link objects in the client's own priority order (the client's configured fallback chain)
client_configured_default.config_search: explicit path, then PODCAST_MODELS_JSON env label, then the shipped config/models.json (model_router.py load_models_config)

selection.on_unresolved_message: No model is configured for this tier. Ask the client which model they want to use for this work, or which model to record as their configured default, then record the answer in the client's models config (client_defaults) and re-run. Never pick a model for the client silently.
